kakheti.name: Kakheti
kakheti.summary: Georgia's main wine region combines warm valley floors, Caucasus influence and a deep qvevri tradition.

saperavi.expect: Deeply colored and structured, with dark fruit, high acidity and firm tannin.

rkatsiteli.expect: High-acid and savory, ranging from crisp white styles to structured amber qvevri wines.

identity.setting: Warm continental valley with mountain influence
identity.terrain: Alazani valley and Caucasus foothills

why.cause: Warm days and cooler mountain-influenced nights
why.effect: Support full ripening while retaining useful acidity.

why.cause: Traditional qvevri fermentation for some wines
why.effect: Can add texture, tannin and savory complexity, especially in skin-contact whites.

santorini.name: Santorini
santorini.summary: Wind, drought and volcanic soils shape intensely fresh Assyrtiko despite the island's heat.

assyrtiko.expect: Bone-dry, powerful and piercingly fresh, with citrus, saline and stony character.

identity.terrain: Volcanic slopes and terraces

why.effect: Keeps wines vivid even in a hot, dry climate.
Favor low yields and concentrated fruit while traditional vine training protects grapes.

naoussa.name: Naoussa
naoussa.summary: Naoussa is the classic home of Xinomavro: pale, high-acid, tannic and famously savory.

xinomavro.expect: High-acid and tannic with sour cherry, tomato-leaf and savory complexity.

identity.terrain: Slopes below Mount Vermio
influences: Cooler nights than southern Greek regions

why.cause: Xinomavro's naturally high tannin and acidity
why.effect: Creates a firm structure that can reward long ageing.
Help preserve perfume and red-fruit freshness.

tokaj.name: Tokaj
tokaj.summary: Furmint combines fierce acidity with orchard fruit and can range from dry mineral wines to legendary sweet styles.

furmint.decant: No decant for young dry styles
furmint.expect: Taut and high-acid with apple, quince and mineral detail; sweetness varies widely by style.

identity.terrain: Volcanic hills above river confluences
influences: Autumn humidity near the Bodrog and Tisza rivers

why.effect: Supports both dry wines and intensely sweet wines without losing freshness.
Can favor noble rot in suitable years for sweet styles.

douro.name: Douro
douro.summary: Steep schist terraces and intense heat create concentrated reds from native Portuguese varieties.

touriga-nacional.expect: Dense, floral and structured, with dark fruit, violet and firm tannin.

identity.terrain: Very steep river terraces

why.effect: Promote deep ripeness and concentration in thick-skinned red grapes.
Often produce small crops with substantial flavor concentration.

canelones.name: Canelones
canelones.summary: Uruguay's signature Tannat combines Atlantic freshness with dark fruit and substantial structure.

tannat.expect: Dark, structured and fresh, with firm tannin, black fruit and savory detail.

identity.terrain: Low rolling hills near Montevideo
influences: Atlantic and Río de la Plata influence

why.effect: Helps Tannat retain acidity alongside ripe dark fruit.
Often makes the traditionally tannic grape more polished and approachable.

vayots-dzor.name: Vayots Dzor
vayots-dzor.summary: High-elevation vineyards produce fragrant, fresh Areni Noir with red fruit and savory spice.

areni-noir.expect: Medium-bodied and aromatic, with bright red fruit, fresh acidity and herbal spice.

identity.terrain: Mountain valleys and volcanic uplands

why.effect: Help preserve acidity and aromatic lift despite strong sunlight.
Reduce disease pressure and support concentrated small berries.

dealu-mare.name: Dealu Mare
dealu-mare.summary: Sunny southern slopes are one of Romania's leading red-wine zones and an important home for Fetească Neagră.

feteasca-neagra.expect: Ripe and spicy with dark fruit, moderate-firm tannin and savory depth.

identity.terrain: Long band of south-facing sub-Carpathian hills

why.effect: Support reliable ripening for structured red varieties.

why.cause: Cooler nights near the Carpathian foothills
why.effect: Help retain freshness and aromatic detail.

tenerife.name: Tenerife / Canary Islands
tenerife.summary: Volcanic island vineyards and altitude give Listán Negro a light, smoky and peppery personality.

listan-negro.expect: Light to medium-bodied, peppery and smoky, with fresh red fruit and bright acidity.

identity.terrain: Volcanic slopes rising from the Atlantic
identity.soil: Young volcanic ash and basaltic material
influences: Phylloxera-free old vines in many sites

why.effect: Temper subtropical warmth and help retain freshness.

why.cause: Low-input old-vine sites on volcanic terrain
why.effect: Often yield distinctive, savory wines with relatively modest body.

cananea-sonora.name: Cananea / Sonora
cananea-sonora.summary: Northern Sonora's high desert vineyards combine intense sunlight with elevation and cool nights, producing ripe but surprisingly fresh reds.

syrah.expect: Full-bodied yet fresh for a desert-grown Syrah, with dark fruit, pepper, violet and savory herbs.

cabernet-sauvignon.expect: Ripe black fruit and firm Cabernet structure, balanced by high-desert freshness and herbal detail.

identity.terrain: Elevated basins and foothills near the Sierra Madre
identity.soil: Rocky, mineral-rich desert soils with low organic matter

why.cause: High elevation and cool desert nights
why.effect: Help retain acidity and aromatic detail despite intense daytime sun.
Support reliable ripening and concentrated fruit when water is carefully managed.

lodi.name: Lodi
lodi.summary: Lodi is one of California's great old-vine strongholds, with historic Zinfandel producing generous fruit, spice and often more freshness than its warm climate suggests.

zinfandel.expect: Juicy and generous, with ripe berry fruit, peppery spice and the supple concentration associated with old head-trained vines.

identity.setting: Warm Mediterranean with cooling Delta breezes
identity.terrain: Broad, low-lying Central Valley vineyards
identity.soil: Deep sandy loam, especially in the Mokelumne River area
influences: Large concentration of old, often own-rooted vines

why.cause: Deep sandy soils and generations of head training
why.effect: Have helped many historic vineyards survive while naturally low yields can build concentration.
Promote ripe fruit while tempering some of the region's daytime heat.

amador.name: Amador County / Sierra Foothills
amador.summary: Gold Country Zinfandel combines intense sunshine and old vines with elevation, giving powerful berry fruit, spice and firmer structure than many valley-floor examples.

zinfandel.expect: Powerful and spicy, with dark berry fruit, elevated alcohol, firmer tannin and a fresher edge from foothill elevation.

identity.terrain: Rolling foothills and elevated Gold Country sites
identity.soil: Decomposed granite, volcanic and sandy loam soils

why.effect: Help preserve acidity alongside fully ripe Zinfandel fruit.
Can produce concentrated wines with substantial spice and structure.

amyndeon.name: Amyndeon
amyndeon.summary: One of Xinomavro's coolest strongholds, Amyndeon emphasizes perfume, bright red fruit and acidity over sheer weight.

xinomavro.expect: Lighter and more aromatic than Naoussa, with vivid acidity, red fruit, rose and savory Xinomavro character.

identity.terrain: Plateau around lakes and mountain basins
identity.soil: Sandy and alluvial soils with limestone influence

why.cause: High altitude and cooler growing conditions
why.effect: Favor bright acidity, perfume and a lighter expression of Xinomavro.
Allows savory varietal character to develop without excessive weight.

drama.name: Drama
drama.summary: Northern Greece gives Assyrtiko a more aromatic, fruit-driven expression than volcanic Santorini while preserving the grape's trademark acidity.

assyrtiko.expect: Fresh and aromatic, with citrus and orchard fruit, less saline austerity than Santorini and a clean high-acid finish.

identity.terrain: Basin and foothill vineyards below mountain ranges
identity.soil: Mixed clay, limestone and alluvial soils

why.cause: Warm days and cooler mountain-influenced nights
why.effect: Support ripe fruit aromas while preserving Assyrtiko's natural freshness.
Often produce a softer, more fruit-led expression than the stark volcanic style associated with Santorini.

madiran.name: Madiran
madiran.summary: Tannat's southwestern French home is structured, dark and savory, typically firmer and less fruit-forward than modern Uruguayan examples.

tannat.expect: Dense, savory and formidable, with dark fruit, high tannin, earthy depth and long ageing potential.

identity.terrain: Rolling foothills near the Pyrenees

why.cause: Tannat's naturally thick skins and high phenolics
why.effect: Give Madiran its formidable tannin and long ageing potential.
Keeps the wines savory and structured rather than purely fruit-driven.

dao.name: Dão
dao.summary: Dão shows Touriga Nacional in a fresher, more floral and restrained register than the hotter Douro.

touriga-nacional.expect: Floral and structured but less massive than Douro, with fresh acidity, dark-red fruit and savory herbal detail.

identity.terrain: Granite uplands surrounded by mountain ranges

why.effect: Allow slow ripening with fresher acidity than Portugal's hottest interior zones.
Are commonly associated with restrained, aromatic reds rather than maximal ripeness.

dragasani.name: Drăgășani
dragasani.summary: Oltenian hills give Fetească Neagră a lifted, fresh expression with red-black fruit, spice and less weight than warmer Dealu Mare examples.

feteasca-neagra.expect: Fresh, spicy and medium-bodied, with red-black fruit and a more lifted profile than richer southern Romanian expressions.

identity.terrain: Rolling hills above the Olt river

why.effect: Help retain acidity and aromatic lift in ripe Fetească Neagră.
Support a balanced style with spice and fruit rather than excessive body.

la-palma.name: La Palma / Canary Islands
la-palma.summary: La Palma adds another volcanic island expression of Listán Negro: bright, peppery and smoky, often from old vines on dramatic slopes.

listan-negro.expect: Light, bright and smoky, with tart red fruit, pepper and savory volcanic-island character.

identity.setting: Subtropical Atlantic island with steep altitude
identity.terrain: Steep volcanic slopes and terraced vineyards
identity.soil: Young volcanic ash, lapilli and basaltic material

why.effect: Temper subtropical warmth and preserve bright acidity.

why.cause: Old vines on steep volcanic terrain
why.effect: Often produce small crops and distinctive savory, smoky associations.

somlo.name: Somló
somlo.summary: Tiny volcanic Somló produces stern, dry Furmint with fierce acidity, restrained fruit and a smoky-stony personality.

furmint.expect: Bone-dry, taut and savory, with apple, quince, smoke and a distinctly firm mineral impression.

identity.terrain: Isolated volcanic hill rising from western Hungary
identity.soil: Basaltic volcanic soils mixed with loess and clay

why.cause: Cool continental conditions and exposed slopes
why.effect: Keep Furmint high in acidity and relatively restrained in fruit.
Highlights Furmint's structure and savory character rather than Tokaj's sweet-wine spectrum.

kartli.name: Kartli
kartli.climate: Continental, drier and cooler than Kakheti
kartli.summary: Central Georgia gives Rkatsiteli a leaner, fresher expression, often emphasizing citrus, herbs and acidity over Kakheti's broader qvevri styles.

rkatsiteli.expect: Crisp and linear, with green apple, citrus and herbs; generally lighter than the broadest Kakhetian expressions.

identity.terrain: River valleys and rolling foothills around the Kura/Mtkvari basin
influences: Mix of modern and traditional winemaking

why.cause: Dry continental conditions and cooler nights
why.effect: Support crisp acidity and a relatively lean expression of Rkatsiteli.

why.cause: A mix of stainless-steel and traditional cellar approaches
why.effect: Produces styles ranging from fresh, citrus-led whites to more textured skin-contact wines.
